title: When to Pre-Train Graph Neural Networks? From Data Generation Perspective!

problem.claim: Graph pre-trained models can suffer from negative transfer on downstream tasks.

gap.claim: Existing work focuses on what and how to pre-train, while some advanced pre-train-and-fine-tune paradigms provide no distinct benefit and do not answer when pre-training is useful.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces W2PGNN, a framework for determining when graph pre-training may benefit downstream tasks.
W2PGNN models pre-training data with graphon bases and defines a generator space from convex combinations of those bases.
The framework addresses application scope, pre-training feasibility, and pre-training data selection.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present W2PGNN as a generic framework that addresses when to pre-train from a data-generation perspective.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a theoretically sound solution for determining the application scope of graph pre-trained models.
The authors report extensive empirical justifications for quantifying pre-training feasibility and selecting pre-training data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph pre-training seeks transferable knowledge from unlabeled graph data to improve downstream performance.
Negative transfer and cases without distinct benefit motivate deciding when pre-training is useful.
W2PGNN analyzes data-generation mechanisms using graphon bases and their convex-combination generator space.
Pre-training feasibility is quantified by the probability of generating downstream data from the generator space.
The framework supports three applications, with theory reported for one and empirical justification reported for two.

source_observation.claim: Pre-training feasibility is framed as the generation probability of downstream data from generators derived from pre-training graph patterns.

interpretation.claim: A useful pre-training decision criterion can be based on compatibility between pre-training and downstream data-generating structures.

application.claim: Before costly pre-training, assess whether downstream data appear reachable from the proposed pre-training generator space.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this criterion applies beyond the described graph pre-training setting.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative empirical results are not specified.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical guarantees or assumptions.
Implementation, computational cost, and limitations are not specified.
